verdictRationale: Task A (SDK first external chain) and Task B (governance propagation timing) both produced real, reproducible measurements against a real one-shot PostgreSQL cluster and the real independent memory-module service over HTTP. Both verdict cells from the Alpha Gate are now satisfied with evidence. One honesty caveat: the independent service at this baseline could not boot as-shipped (a required module was deleted upstream but its import was left behind); a temporary no-op shim was added to boot it and is removed at cleanup. See honestyNotes.

propagationTimings.method: For each op: issue governance HTTP request, measure API latency (request->response). Then poll the relevant derived table via psql until consistent, measuring settlement lag (response -> derived consistent). 3 samples/op, median reported. Derived faces are written synchronously inside repository.save() (full-aggregate overwrite) BEFORE the 200 is returned, so measured settlement (~15ms) reflects psql poll round-trip overhead, not server-side delay.

pin.outboxNote: pin does NOT emit a new memory_outbox_events row (3012ms = observation timeout, i.e. no emission) -- not a failure

revoke.outboxNote: revoke does NOT emit a new memory_outbox_events row (3008ms timeout = no emission)

forget.outboxNote: forget marks pre-existing outbox rows redacted; does not emit a NEW aggregate outbox row (3003ms timeout)

delete.outboxNote: delete does NOT emit a new memory_outbox_events row (3010ms timeout = no emission)

derivedFaceStatus.index (index_documents): 0 rows throughout the run. The canonical index builder is the (deleted) service-worker module; with the no-op shim it never runs, and memory-module.governance ops only REMOVE index rows (no-op on an empty table). NOT exercised by this lane.
derivedFaceStatus.episode (episodes): 0 rows; hold() does not create episodes and these ops only remove them. NOT exercised.
derivedFaceStatus.profile (profile_snapshot_items): 0 rows for the tested tenant/user; these ops only prune them. NOT exercised by this lane.
derivedFaceStatus.cache (memory_cache): No canonical memory_cache table exists at this baseline (Redis not configured). N/A.
derivedFaceStatus.outbox (memory_outbox_events): Real and exercised: only 'correct' emits a new 'assertion.active' row (settles synchronously, ~30ms); pin/revoke/forget/delete do not emit a new aggregate outbox row.

forget_non_resurrection.detail: after forget, memory_assertions.status stayed 'forgotten' (never back to 'active'), index_documents stayed 0, memory_tombstones row persisted across a 1500ms poll window

delete_non_resurrection.detail: after delete, memory_assertions row stayed absent, index_documents stayed 0, memory_tombstones row persisted across 1500ms poll window

control_subject_survives.detail: a separate control memory (tenant lane-t / user lane-u) created before all samples remained status='active' and untombstoned after all operations

no_production_touch.detail: only /tmp/cochpia-mem-5496 (port 5496, trust) used; port 5433 and repo .env never referenced

honestyNotes: TEMPORARY SHIM REQUIRED TO BOOT THE SERVICE: at baseline c76cfb9, services/memory-module/index.js imports server/memory-module-service-worker.js, but that module was deleted upstream in commit d3a6d81 ('refactor(core-v0): R-020 stage 4 - delete unused endpoints and dead modules') without updating the import. The service cannot start as-shipped. A temporary no-op shim (server/memory-module-service-worker.js, untracked) was added so the lane could run; it is DELETED during cleanup and never committed. This is a real baseline defect, not a measurement artifact.

INDEXER GAP: because the real service-worker (which builds index_documents from outbox 'assertion.active' events) is missing, index_documents stayed at 0 rows. The SDK smoke's read-your-write still passed -- its retrieve path does not depend on the BM25 index (it resolves the just-written memory via the assertion/consistency-token read path). So the external chain is proven working, but the production indexer path is currently a no-op and would matter for BM25 retrieval at scale.

OUTBOX MEASUREMENT: only 'correct' emits a new memory_outbox_events row; the ~3000ms 'outbox' value for pin/revoke/forget/delete is the poll timeout meaning 'no new outbox row emitted', which is correct behavior, not a failure.

PROPAGATION LAG INTERPRETATION: governance derived faces are written synchronously inside the same save() transaction that returns the 200, so the ~15ms 'derived settle' is psql poll round-trip overhead; true server-side convergence is sub-ms. Reported honestly as observed wall-clock.
NO FABRICATION: every number is from a real run; nothing synthesized.
